subject: Post-demo: model routing runbook & integration clarifications
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: model routing runbook & integration clarifications

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Per our call, I put together the high-level runbook below to capture the integration and routing items we discussed. Attaching a draft runbook and our latency SLA matrix for reference.

Key goals you mentioned
- Keep avg token latency under 350ms for triage flow (peak expected 25rps)
- Tight budget target: $0.0008/token for the majority of user-facing traffic
- Strict PHI handling for a subset of requests (redaction + private deployment on premise possible later)

Proposal (high level) — integration & routing
1) SDK & auth
   - Use server-side Redwood SDK (Node or Python) so BrightLeaf frontends never hold inference API keys.
   - Auth: short-lived JWTs issued by BrightLeaf auth service + Redwood token exchange for session-scoped keys. For high-security routes, we recommend mTLS to Redwood Private (if you go on-prem/VPC).

2) Model routing and policy (how requests move between variants)
   - Primary: gpt-xl-lowlat (latency-optimized) for 90% of real-time triage traffic.
   - Fallback 1: gpt-xl-cost (quantized variant) when queue > 500ms or cost threshold reached.
   - Fallback 2: gpt-l1-short for non-critical bulk/async jobs.
   - Routing rules expressed as simple policy: latency_budget_ms, cost_per_token_budget, region_preference. Example: if end-to-end > 350ms -> route to gpt-xl-cost for next N requests, with circuit-breaker back to primary when healthy.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - Use Redwood tool-calling to surface structured JSON for triage results (intent, severity, suggested next-steps).
   - Keep a strict schema; we recommend validating on the SDK layer and failing gracefully to a safe text fallback if JSON parsing fails.

4) Embeddings + reranker
   - Use embeddings for candidate retrieval from patient notes (faiss index).
   - Use a light reranker (2-3 candidates) with a reranker model that trades small latency ~20-40ms for higher precision.

5) Observability & ops
   - Per-route token breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and a routing decision log to help tune thresholds.

Open questions for you
- Which flows require strict PHI separation (we discussed triage vs autopopulate)?
- Do you want region pinning for EU patients now, or plan that for phase 2?

Next steps
- Share this draft runbook (attached) with your engineering/security teams.
- Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead (Lumi) next week? We can walk through SDK auth, the routing policy DSL, and run a short latency test.

Attachments: redwood-model-routing-runbook-draft.pdf, latency-sla-matrix.xlsx

--
Priya Natarajan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Priya — this is super helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

> Which flows require strict PHI separation (we discussed triage vs autopopulate)?

We consider triage contained PHI (names, small notes) and would need to ensure retention controls and audit logging. Autopopulate (template suggestions) is non-PHI. We'll likely need Private deployment for triage in the medium term.

On routing:
- Are fallbacks circuit-breaker based (i.e., we failover automatically at X latency) or request-by-request? We prefer circuit-breaker behavior so we don't keep hitting a slow model.

On SDK:
- Can you send a minimal Node snippet showing the JWT exchange + request path? Also want an example of structured output validation on our side.

Security:
- Our InfoSec wants to understand audit logs and whether we can get raw request metadata (no content) for compliance.

We're good to do a deep-dive. Lumi is available Thursday 17 Sep 10–11am PT or Monday 21 Sep 2–3pm PT. Which works for you/your engineer?

Thanks,
Marta
Director, Product Ops
BrightLeaf Health
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@brightleafhealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model routing runbook & integration clarifications

Hi Marta — quick answers and a tiny sample. Happy to expand in the deep-dive.

Circuit breaker behavior
- We recommend a circuit-breaker at the routing layer: evaluate a sliding window of p50/p95 latency + error rate. If p95 > latency_budget or errors > 2% for window T, flip traffic to fallback for a cooldown period and probe periodically. This prevents continuous retries to a degraded variant.

Minimal Node snippet (JWT exchange -> call)
```js
// exchange short-lived BrightLeaf JWT for Redwood session token
const axios = require('axios');
async function getRedwoodSession(brightleafJwt) {
  const res = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/sessions/exchange', {
    jwt: brightleafJwt
  });
  return res.data.session_token; // short-lived
}

async function callInference(sessionToken, prompt) {
  const res = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
    model: 'gpt-xl-lowlat',
    prompt,
    routing_policy: {
      latency_budget_ms: 350,
      fallback_chain: ['gpt-xl-cost','gpt-l1-short'],
      region_preference: 'us-east-1'
    },
    structured_output: { schema_version: 'v1', required: ['intent','severity'] }
  }, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${sessionToken}` }
  });
  return res.data;
}
```

Structured output validation example (server-side)
- Validate JSON schema before storing. If validation fails, return a safe free-text result and log the event to routing decision logs.

Audit logs / metadata
- We can provide request metadata (timestamp, routing decision, model_variant, token_count) without storing user content. For strict PHI flows we recommend Private deployment and customer-managed KMS so logs can be routed into your SIEM.

I'll bring a prototype routing config and a tiny load script to the deep-dive so we can run a real 10–15 minute latency exercise.

--
